text:
Lamar Jackson is out. The Ravens have ruled him out of Sunday night in Atlanta, so Snoop Huntley starts against a Falcons team that is reportedly feeling confident with Michael Penix Jr. at quarterback. Jesse Minter says he expects Huntley to play well, which is what anyone would say about the backup on Saturday. It gets worse. Cam Jurgens is out with a concussion, Trey Hendrickson has gone from questionable to out with his finger, Ja'Kobi Lane is on injured reserve and Zay Flowers is questionable with a foot. Yesterday this column trusted the gloomy Sunday price over the cheerful February one, and that call looks healthier than Baltimore's roster. Oddly, the line has come in from +3.5 to +3. My guess is the market had already assumed Lamar wouldn't play. Rob and Darren hold four Baltimore tickets between them. I would not want any of them this weekend.

Andy's candle has been snuffed out. Brian Branch is out with an Achilles, and Rock Ya-Sin and Ben Bartch are out too. That leaves a Lions secondary I wouldn't trust against a stiff breeze. Detroit is still giving 5.5 at Arizona, and I think that's too many.

Darren is now on the third chapter of his tragedy. Kyle Dugger is out and Bryan Cook is questionable, so the Bengals are short at safety on top of everything else. Steve, meanwhile, has no new names on Kansas City's injury list for a second day running. He is 4-0 and doing absolutely nothing, which is the most annoying thing a man can do in a pool.

The Ravens opened this week as 4.5-point favourites in Atlanta. They are now 3-point underdogs. That is a seven-and-a-half-point swing, and it lands on a team with Lamar Jackson questionable with his ankle and Marlon Humphrey questionable with a calf. Trey Hendrickson and John Simpson are questionable too, and tight end Durham Smythe has gone to injured reserve with an Achilles. Oddly, the title market has nudged Baltimore in to +850. So the bookies believe in the Ravens for February but not for Sunday night. I'm with the Sunday version. Rob and Darren each hold Baltimore in two bets, and both should be watching Michael Penix Jr. and Bijan Robinson through their fingers.

Darren has it worst, because his other team is Cincinnati. Dexter Lawrence II and B.J. Hill are now questionable on the defensive line, on top of the receiver mess we covered yesterday. Two horses, both limping, and Darren is holding the reins of each.

Andy is having the quietest good week in the pool. The Lions have come back in from +2800 to +2600, and the line at Arizona has firmed from 4.5 to 5.5. Cade Mays is listed on injured reserve, so nobody should start engraving anything. Still, yesterday's flicker of hope has become a modest candle, which by Andy's standards is a bonfire. And Steve? Nothing to report again. The Chiefs are 4-0 with no new names on the injury list, and his feet are still up. Someone should check he's still breathing.

The Ravens answered Lamar's wobbly ankle by trading for two-time Pro Bowl center Cam Jurgens from the Eagles, and Jason Kelce says he's excited to see him back at center. Lovely. The snag is that Jurgens is on Baltimore's injury list, questionable with a concussion. So Rob and Darren's big reinforcement arrives in the same condition as the rest of that building. Zay Flowers, Rashod Bateman and Kyle Hamilton have joined the questionable pile too. I like the trade for January. I don't trust it for Sunday night against Bijan Robinson.

Darren, about that line yesterday's column told you to savour. Ja'Marr Chase is questionable with a concussion, Tee Higgins is questionable with a groin injury, and Cincinnati has slipped from 7-point favourites at Miami back to 6.5. My read is that's the receivers showing up in the price. The Bengals have also drifted out to +1900 for the title. Rob's Chiefs bet against those Bengals was the healthiest thing he owned yesterday. Today it's healthier still.

Andy gets a flicker of hope: the Lions have opened the practice window for Brian Branch and Cade Mays, though Branch is still listed out. Then Sam LaPorta announced that his extension talks are at a "stalemate," and the title market pushed Detroit out to +2800. Andy sits under 30% in all three of his bets. Meanwhile Steve's Chiefs are 4-0 and shortening to +900, and their only new injury worry is a questionable tackle. Steve hasn't had to do anything all week, and it's going perfectly.

Lamar Jackson has a sprained ankle, and sources told NFL Network he has only an outside chance of playing Sunday against the Falcons. Yesterday nobody could say whether he'd play. Now somebody has, and it's not what Rob and Darren wanted to hear. The Ravens opened as 4.5-point favourites in Atlanta and are now 3.5-point underdogs, and my read is that this is the Lamar news showing up in the line. On top of that, Durham Smythe is out with an Achilles, and Trey Hendrickson and Chris Moore are both questionable. The title market moved the Ravens from +900 to +850 since Sunday. I wouldn't treat that as a vote of confidence until it survives this week.

Steve is the winner here without lifting a finger. Steve has the 4-0 Chiefs against the Ravens in two bets, and the other team just lost its quarterback to an ankle. Andy also holds two bets against Baltimore. That 30% against Darren now looks less like charity and more like a lottery ticket that's started to tingle. Yesterday this column told Rob to pick a lane. Fate has picked it for him, and his Chiefs bet against Darren is now the healthiest thing he owns.

Darren is quietly doomed. Darren holds the Ravens in two bets and the Bengals against Rob, and Stephen A. is asking out loud why Zac Taylor isn't under more scrutiny. Cincinnati has gone from 5.5-point to 7-point favourites at Miami. That's the only line on this page moving Darren's way, so savour it, Darren. And keep the Falcons tape handy, though it may now be a horror film.

Tyreek Hill is a free agent. His agent, Drew Rosenhaus, says Hill could sign somewhere "over the next few days," and the Chiefs are believed to be interested. Kansas City has been following his rehab since before Tyquan Thornton dislocated his ankle, which now means 12 to 16 weeks out, and before Rashee Rice went questionable with a hamstring. Nothing is signed yet. The bookies have still nudged the Chiefs from +950 to +900, and my hunch is that a 4-0 team adding a familiar speed merchant is the scariest thing on this page. Steve holds Kansas City in three bets and should start pricing a new jersey. Rob holds the Chiefs against Darren, which is lovely, and is backing the Ravens against Steve's Chiefs, which is awkward. Pick a lane, Rob.

Darren is the most likely to spill the coffee. Darren is against the Chiefs in two bets, and the Ravens, Darren's other hope, still can't say whether Lamar Jackson plays Sunday night against Atlanta. Tee Higgins is day-to-day, which by Bengals standards this week counts as good news. Yesterday's advice to watch Falcons tape stands.

Andy, Dan Campbell is changing nothing on a defense that just lost to the Panthers, Rock Ya-Sin is doubtful, and the Lions have slid again to +2400. Loyalty is admirable, but in my opinion it isn't a pass rush. The market gives you 30% in all three of your bets, and I think that's generous.

Lamar Jackson left Sunday's game with an ankle injury, and Jamison Hensley reports he could miss next week's game against the Falcons. Four of the six bets ride on the Ravens, two for Rob and two for Darren, and the man holding all four up just limped off. Trey Hendrickson is out with a finger injury, and Ronnie Stanley and Marlon Humphrey are questionable. Meanwhile the bookies shortened Baltimore's title price from +900 to +850. I can't tell you whether that happened before or after the ankle news, so I won't pretend to. My view is that the Ravens without Lamar are a decent team with a very bad week coming, and Rob and Darren should start watching Falcons tape.

Now for a called shot that blew up. Yesterday this column backed the Raiders' unbeaten run against Mahomes at Allegiant. The Chiefs won 30-27, they're 4-0, and Mahomes still hasn't lost there. Steve, go ahead and gloat. The cost was Tyquan Thornton, who dislocated his ankle and is out. Steve is sitting pretty, and so is Rob on the Kansas City side of things.

Darren, your Bengals lost to Jacksonville. Ja'Marr Chase is questionable with a concussion, Tee Higgins is questionable with a groin injury, and the whole internet has watched Travis Hunter juke Higgins. Cincinnati has drifted out to +1900. Andy, the Lions drifted to +2200 overnight and my notes don't say why. I think that's somehow worse.

Rob, Darren, remember yesterday's confident line about the Ravens' side of the Andy bets looking the healthier one? Baltimore put centre Ethan Pocic and guard Jovaughn Gwyn on injured reserve this morning, and receiver Chris Moore joined Zay Flowers as questionable. That takes two pieces out of the interior of the offensive line in one go, and four of the six bets ride on this team. Oddly, the bookies don't care. Baltimore is an 11.5-point favourite over Tennessee after opening at 8.5, and I can't tell you when the line moved compared with the injury news, so I won't pretend it's connected. My view is that a team that has to work out who its centre is couldn't ask for a gentler opponent than these Titans.

Andy, the Lions and Sam LaPorta have broken off contract talks. Nobody's hurt. Your star tight end just goes into tonight's game at Carolina with his next contract on his mind. Players in that spot either play out of their skin or sulk. I'm calling the first, mostly out of pity.

Steve, the Chiefs have drifted from 5.5-point to 4.5-point favourites at Las Vegas. My read is that the market is pricing in Josh Simmons being out, since he was ruled out mid-week. Mahomes is 6-0 at Allegiant and the Raiders are unbeaten, so something has to give. My money's on the Raiders' unbeaten run. Spare a thought for Rob, who holds the Chiefs against Darren and holds the Ravens against Steve's Chiefs, so he's rooting for Kansas City and against it on the same Sunday.

Andy, the vibes have taken a hit. Brian Branch, the Lions safety, is out with an Achilles injury, and guard Ben Bartch was ruled out this morning too. Cornerback D.J. Reed is questionable with his ribs. Yesterday I called my pick of your Lions over Rob's Ravens shrewd because Carolina had no starting cornerbacks. Today Detroit is missing pieces of its own secondary. The bookies barely blinked and nudged the Lions from 3 to 3.5 points favourites in Carolina. I'm less relaxed. You're the underdog in all three of your bets, and this isn't the week that changes it.

Rob and Darren don't get to gloat for long. Baltimore's top pass rusher, Trey Hendrickson, had surgery on a broken finger and misses Tennessee. Ronnie Stanley is questionable with a toe and Zay Flowers with a hamstring. My hunch is that a finger mends faster than an Achilles, which is why the Ravens' side of the Andy bets still looks the healthier one. But that's a hunch, not a doctor's note.

Steve, the stiff back I mentioned yesterday has turned into a ruling: Josh Simmons is out at Las Vegas. Darren, Kyle Dugger is out and Bryan Cook is questionable, so yesterday's rumour of a secondary is now a vacancy. Meanwhile Rob is the favourite in all three of his bets and is insufferable about it. That's how I'd read his silence, anyway.

Steve, the Chiefs are drifting. The line at Las Vegas opened at 5.5 and now sits at 4.5. In the meantime Kansas City has added offensive tackle Josh Simmons to the injury list with a bad back, and L'Jarius Sneed is still questionable with a knee. My read is that the market noticed the man who protects Mahomes walking stiffly. The Raiders, meanwhile, have started fast enough that people have stopped calling their ground Arrowhead West. A one-point move isn't a crisis, and 3-0 is still 3-0. But Steve has staked three bets on this team without a flicker of doubt, and this is the first week the bookies have shown one.

Rob, you're on Kansas City too, against Darren. Don't laugh at Steve too loudly. Darren, your Bengals have now added cornerback DJ Turner II to that list of questionable safeties, so it isn't so much a secondary as a rumour. Your one comfort is that Burrow has never lost to Trevor Lawrence. I'd want more than that to lean on.

Andy, the Panthers will play Goff without either starting cornerback. That makes my vibes pick of your Lions over Rob's Ravens look shrewder by the day. Rob and Darren can console themselves that Derrick Henry is finally on their side against Tennessee, with Baltimore favoured by 11.5. That is a big number for a team that keeps losing at home.

Rob, Darren: Lamar Jackson is on the injury list with a bad back and is questionable for Sunday. Yesterday this column joked that the bookies had decided Lamar didn't need blockers. This morning the question is whether Lamar needs a heat pad. He has company. Zay Flowers and Marlon Humphrey have hamstrings, Ronnie Stanley has a toe and Trey Hendrickson has a finger, all on top of the two linemen already out. The Ravens have also lost four straight games in Baltimore. The line against Tennessee still reads 11.5, so the bookies are unbothered. I'm bothered on your behalf. Between you, you hold Baltimore in four bets, and that's a lot of eggs in one sore-backed basket.

Andy, this is the best news you've had all season, and you did nothing to earn it. You're at 40% against Darren's Ravens, and my hunch is that number is already out of date. My vibes pick of Lions over Rob's Ravens is starting to look less like spite and more like scouting. Don't get smug, though: Detroit just put centre Cade Mays on injured reserve.

Darren, Cincinnati's casualty list now includes three safeties, Bryan Cook, Jordan Battle and Kyle Dugger, all questionable. The secondary has gone from a problem to a vacancy. Steve, meanwhile, is reading McCourty confess he feels like an idiot for doubting Mahomes. Steve has never doubted anything in his life, which is its own kind of foolishness, but at 3-0 it's working beautifully.

Darren, the Bengals have found the problem, and it was one punt. Ke'Shawn Williams muffed it, the mistake led to Pittsburgh's 30-27 win, and by Tuesday he'd been cut and replaced by Mitch Tinsley. It's decisive, and it misses the point. The same week, cornerback Jalen Davis went on injured reserve with a hamstring, which leaves a secondary that Stephen A. already rates as a problem. Cincinnati are only 2.5-point favourites at home to Jacksonville, which is the market shrugging politely. Rob is 57% in that bet with an unbeaten Chiefs team, and I think that's generous to Darren.

Rob, your week is stranger. Jovaughn Gwyn has joined Ethan Pocic on the out list, so the offensive line is now mostly tape. Yet the Ravens' line against Tennessee has moved from 8.5 to 11.5. Either the bookies think very little of the Titans, or they've decided Lamar doesn't need blockers. I lean toward the second, and so, clearly, does Darren, whose two Baltimore bets suddenly look less like a liability.

Steve, the Chiefs have slipped from 5.5 to 4.5 at Las Vegas, and tackle Josh Simmons went on the list with a bad back. My read is that the two are connected. At 3-0, you'll live. Andy, safety Christian Izien starred for the Lions last week, and they're 3.5-point favourites at Carolina. You're still stuck under 40% in every bet. I'm sticking with yesterday's vibes pick, Lions over Rob's Ravens, mostly because I enjoy watching you both sweat.

Rob, the Rio hangover has arrived, and it's standing where your center used to be. The Ravens lost two centers in that Dallas win. Ethan Pocic is out with a knee, and the plan for Tennessee may be a rookie guard, Vega Ioane, snapping to Lamar Jackson. Add yesterday's Ronnie Stanley toe and that line is held together with tape and hope. Solak is floating Lamar for MVP this morning. I'd settle for Lamar upright on Sunday. Darren, wipe off the smirk: two of your three bets ride on that same wobbly snap.

Andy, your Lions just hung 31 points for a record third straight week to open the season, and they did it while their own center, Cade Mays, went to injured reserve and Ben Bartch was ruled out. The difference is that Detroit seems to score no matter who's standing up front. You're still only 40% in all three bets. I'm starting to think that number is a clerical error, and I'm taking the Lions over Rob's Ravens on vibes alone.

Darren, the Bengals lost B.J. Hill to an Achilles and Colbie Young to a knee, and Stephen A. says the defense is still a problem. When Stephen A. and I agree, it's a bad week. Steve, the juiciest Chiefs-tagged item this morning is Matthew Stafford turning up in a Taylor Swift music video. At 3-0, you can afford to be upstaged.

Rob, you had the kind of Sunday people lie about at barbecues. The Ravens beat Dallas in Rio in the final seconds. Tyler Loop got his redemption, and the Cowboys helped with a late fourth-quarter decision I would love to hear someone defend. Your Chiefs beat Miami 24-10, and Darren's Bengals lost. You're the favourite in all three of your bets, and every one of them went your way. Yesterday I called that Rio pitch a hazard, and Lamar then had one of the big stat days of the week on it. I'll eat that. The only bruise is Ronnie Stanley, now out with a toe injury, and that's Darren's problem too.

Darren, yesterday I said somebody liked your Bengals more than I did. They went to Pittsburgh as 3.5-point favourites, made special teams gaffes, lost a late Burrow fumble and, in the headline's words, couldn't "close it out." I take no pleasure in this. Some pleasure. Your Ravens did carry your other two bets, which is the only reason you're still speaking to Rob.

Steve, I watched that spread slip for two days. Then the Chiefs won by 14, and Mahomes went 14 for 14 on play-action. Consider my eye withdrawn. Andy, Jahmyr Gibbs is getting Barry Sanders comparisons, and you're still the underdog in all three bets. Enjoy the highlight reel.

Andy, your Lions are shopping. ESPN reports Detroit is one of a handful of teams asking the Steelers about cornerback Joey Porter Jr. The news comes with safety Thomas Harper just placed on injured reserve. Nobody has been traded, and asking isn't buying. Still, when a contender starts ringing around for defensive backs in September, I read that as a secondary that knows it's short. Detroit's title price has drifted from +1800 to +2000, and you're the underdog in all three of your bets. It's a shopping trip, Andy, not a rescue.

Rob and Darren, the league has had another look at the Rio grass and says there's "no need to worry." This column called that pitch a hazard, and I'll take the NFL's word when Lamar walks off it in one piece. The market is calmer than I am. This morning Baltimore went from a 3-point to a 3.5-point favourite over Dallas, even with Zay Flowers still questionable. Darren, your Bengals are also in the injury news: receiver Andrei Iosivas is on injured reserve and defensive tackle B.J. Hill is doubtful. Even so, Cincinnati is now a 3.5-point favourite at Pittsburgh after opening at 1.5. Somebody likes your team more than I do.

Steve, yesterday I said half a point wasn't a crisis. This morning the Chiefs slipped another half point, to 9.5 in Miami. It's still not a crisis. But that's two days in a row, and I'm keeping an eye on you.

Rob and Darren, put the coffee down. Ravens tackle Ronnie Stanley has been ruled out with a toe injury, so Baltimore takes Lamar Jackson to Rio without him. The Maracanã pitch is one that NFL and players' union field experts have spent days inspecting. When the union chief has to put out a lengthy statement about the grass, I'd call that a hazard, not a field. Zay Flowers is still questionable with a hamstring. Between you, you hold Baltimore in four bets. You're 60% in the two against Andy and 49% in the two against Steve. If I were you, I'd watch the first series through my fingers.

Andy, don't get smug. Yesterday this column named Ben Bartch as one of four questionable Lions linemen. Today he's out, and safety Thomas Harper is out with him. Detroit is still only a 6.5-point favourite over the Jets, three points less than at the open. Both Ravens-versus-Lions bets now come down to whose offensive line is held together with more tape. I still take Baltimore, on the theory that Lamar can outrun a missing tackle and nobody on your side can.

Steve is the favourite in all three of his bets. The Chiefs' title price has shortened, and Andy Reid gives rookie corner Mansoor Delane a "good chance" of playing in Miami. The line did slip from 10.5 to 10 today. Half a point is not a crisis. Steve's only real problem is that he has nothing to worry about, which is usually when this column starts watching him.

Andy, yesterday this column called Detroit's quiet week a triumph. It lasted a day. Four Lions offensive linemen were listed questionable today: guards Ben Bartch, Christian Mahogany and Tate Ratledge, and tackle Blake Miller. The line against the Jets has slid from Detroit -9.5 at the open to -6.5. I can't tell you when it moved, but my read is that the market saw the same injury report I did. Dan Campbell says he still has faith in defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard. That would be more soothing if Campbell hadn't demoted offensive coordinators mid-season in two of his previous five years. Andy is behind in all three of his bets, and his best chance is 40%. Yesterday Aaron Glenn knew where the weak spots were. Today they have names.

Darren, Cincinnati is heading the other way. The Bengals opened as 1.5-point favourites at Pittsburgh and are now 3.5-point favourites, and their title price has shortened. The biggest drama in Cincinnati is Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins disputing a fine for a celebration. A team whose main complaint is being charged for having fun is a team in a good mood. Rob, your 53% against Darren's Bengals looks generous to me.

Steve, Stephen A. is backing your Chiefs to win the AFC. I'd treat that endorsement like a questionable calf. Rob and Darren, the Rio line has moved toward Baltimore despite the Ravens' injury list. The market is as relaxed as Lamar. I'm not.

Rob and Darren, your Ravens are flying to Rio with a medical ward in the hold. Seven Baltimore players are now questionable: Ronnie Stanley (toe, added today), Trey Hendrickson, Malaki Starks, Chris Moore and three more, on top of the Zay Flowers we already mentioned. Lamar Jackson calls it a business trip and says he isn't worried about the Maracanã pitch. Lovely. The two of you hold Baltimore in four bets, and both of your bets against Steve are sitting at 50%. I'd be less relaxed than Lamar.

Steve, I need to correct yesterday's coronation. I said nothing on the Kansas City injury list explained the market falling for your team. Since then Chris Jones, L'Jarius Sneed and Felix Anudike-Uzomah have all been listed questionable, and today the Miami line slipped from 11.5 back to 10.5. My read is that the market noticed. It isn't a crisis. Kelce leads the league in yards after catch and is running his fastest routes since 2022. You've gone from insufferable to merely smug.

Darren, your quiet good position has sprung a leak. Andrei Iosivas is expected to miss four to six weeks with a thumb injury, and B.J. Hill and Jonathan Allen are both questionable. Rob, that helps your Chiefs bet, the one bet where the Ravens' injuries can't hurt you. Andy, nothing new has gone wrong in Detroit, which by this column's standards is a triumph. Aaron Glenn is coming back to face his old team, though, and I suspect he still remembers where the weak spots are.

Andy, the bookmakers have found a new way to be rude to you. The Lions opened as 9.5-point favourites at home to the Jets and are now 6.5. That's three points gone against the Jets, a team nobody has ever accused of being frightening. The drop lines up with Blake Miller and Christian Mahogany going on the injury list, so my read is that the market doesn't trust what's left in front of the quarterback. In fairness, I told you yesterday those two were out, and the list actually says questionable. Enjoy that correction, because it's the only thing in this column going your way. You're down to 36% against Steve, and I still think all your numbers are flattering you.

Steve, meanwhile, the Chiefs have gone from 7-point favourites in Miami to 11.5, and there's nothing on the Kansas City injury list to explain it. The market has simply decided it likes your team, and you hold them in three bets. Insufferable Steve is back, and fully earned.

Rob, that same move helps your Chiefs bet against Darren, but don't relax. The Bengals have gone from 1.5 to 3.5-point favourites in Pittsburgh and shortened to +1700, and Zac Taylor is out praising Dexter Lawrence. Darren sits at 47% in that bet, which looks like the quietest good position in the pool. And to both Ravens holders: Zay Flowers is listed questionable, which is more than yesterday's column gave him.

Andy, yesterday I said the best day of your week was the one the Lions spent not playing. I'd like to withdraw that as too generous. Avonte Maddox is out for the season with a foot injury. Two offensive linemen, Blake Miller and Christian Mahogany, are listed out. And Dan Campbell spent the day defending his defensive coordinator, Kelvin Sheppard. The reports are already calling this defence "embattled," and when a head coach has to stand up for his DC before Week 3, the defence is the story. The market pushed Detroit out to +2000, the longest price of our four teams. You hold the Lions in three bets and you're the underdog in all three, at 38%, 38% and 37%. My hunch is those numbers are still being polite.

Steve, I owe you a small correction. I said the market wasn't impressed by the Chiefs needing overtime against the Colts. By this morning it had changed its mind and brought them back in to +1200, and the reporting credits Mahomes with using play action to great effect. That's exactly where they were before Sunday, so I'll call it a draw and never mention it again.

Rob and Darren, your Ravens are off to Rio to play the Cowboys, and the NFL says it has "no concerns" about the field. The Ravens say they aren't worried either. With Flowers out, it's nice to hear there's one thing in Baltimore nobody is worried about.

The Ravens were 8.5-point favourites over the Saints yesterday, took a lead into the fourth quarter, and lost. The headline says "another collapse," and the locker room spent the evening declining to compare itself to past Ravens teams, which is what you do when the comparison is obvious. I said yesterday that the bill for that roster arrives in January. I was wrong, because it came in September. Zay Flowers is out, and so are Nnamdi Madubuike (neck) and Teddye Buchanan (ACL). T.J. Tampa is on injured reserve and Ronnie Stanley has a questionable toe. The title price drifted from +900 to +950. Rob and Darren, you hold four Baltimore bets between you, the numbers still favour you in all of them, and I don't believe any of it.

Darren, I asked for the Bengals medicine back on loan. You can have it back, with interest. Cincinnati beat Houston and is 2-0, and the talk this morning is that the defence might be Super Bowl-calibre. The Bengals were the only one of our four teams whose price shortened, from +1800 to +1700. B.J. Hill is out with an Achilles, which is a real loss. Even so, Rob's 52% now looks flattering to Rob.

Steve, the Chiefs beat the Colts 33-30 in overtime. Kenneth Walker III had 178 all-purpose yards and Butker won it from 40. The market's response was to push them out from +1200 to +1300. My read is that it watched a 6-point favourite need overtime and wasn't impressed. Andy, the Lions didn't play and still drifted to +1800. I called it the best day of your week, and I stand by that.

Yesterday I ate my medicine over Joe Burrow's back. This morning the back is on the injury list again: Burrow is questionable for Houston, listed today. The Bengals have also gone from 2.5-point underdogs to 3, and that moved today too. My read is that those two things are connected. The last word we had was a full practice on Friday and a man set to start, and I have nothing saying that has changed, so I won't pretend to know more. But Darren, I handed you that one twenty-four hours ago and I'd like it back, at least on loan. Rob, your 52% still looks stingy to me. I said that once, retracted it, and am now saying it again, which makes me about as reliable as that back.

Steve, something finally happened to you. Chris Jones is questionable with a calf, rookie corner Mansoor Delane is questionable with a shoulder, and the Chiefs slipped from 6.5-point favourites over the Colts to 6 on the day those two were listed. It's half a point, and my hunch is it means nothing. After two days of having no news at all, though, you may find you preferred it that way.

Zay Flowers went from doubtful to out, which surprised nobody who read yesterday's column. Rob and Darren, the Ravens are still 8.5-point favourites and you're still favoured in all four of your Baltimore bets. I still think the bill for that roster arrives in January. Andy, the Lions aren't playing today, so nothing can go wrong for you, and I'd call this the best day of your week.

Zay Flowers is doubtful for Sunday after aggravating that left hamstring and missing most of the week's practices. Nnamdi Madubuike is out with a neck injury, and T.J. Tampa joined the out list this morning with a knee. Trey Hendrickson is now questionable with a finger, of all things. So naturally the Ravens have gone from 7.5-point favourites over New Orleans to 8.5, and their title price has shortened from +920 to +900. My read is that the market is telling you what it thinks of the Saints, not that it missed Flowers limping. Rob and Darren, you share this team across four bets and you're favoured in all four. Enjoy it, but my hunch is that a roster shedding bodies at this rate sends the bill in January. They're wearing all white on Sunday. Matches the bandages.

Now, my medicine. Yesterday I said, loudly, that 52% for Rob over Darren's Bengals looked stingy, and I was leaning on Joe Burrow's questionable back. Burrow then practised in full on Friday and is set to start in Houston. Darren, that one's yours. Rob, I've been shouting on your behalf with no ammunition. Cincinnati is still a 2.5-point underdog and I still prefer the Chiefs, but it's a coin flip and I'll call it one.

Andy, the only Lions news is the title price drifting from +1900 to +2000. No fresh names on the injury list. The market just thought about Detroit a bit longer. Steve, nothing happened to you. Again.

Jack Campbell fought back tears last night and took the blame for Detroit's defense. He's an All-Pro linebacker and he wasn't the one covering all five Josh Allen touchdowns, so I admire the man and fear for the unit. When your best defender is crying at the podium in Week 2, my read is that the problem is bigger than one man's conscience. Andy, you hold this defense in all three of your bets and you're the underdog in every one: 35% against Darren, 42% against Steve, and Rob sitting at 65% against you. The one scrap of comfort is that Avonte Maddox is listed as questionable with that foot rather than anything worse. Blake Miller and Christian Mahogany are both out, though, so the offensive line is thinning now too. My opinion: quietly doomed, and not that quietly.

Steve, the sloth strategy keeps paying. The Chiefs opened as 5.5-point favourites over Indianapolis and the line has grown to 6.5, with Chris Jones's calf still questionable. My read is the market has looked at that calf and shrugged. You've done nothing all week and your price improved. Infuriating.

Rob and Darren, the Ravens' waiting room got two new patients this morning: guard John Simpson (groin) and Ronnie Stanley (toe), both questionable. Baltimore is still laying 7.5 against New Orleans, so nobody's panicking. I'd just like Lamar's bodyguards to be able to walk. Darren, your Bengals are 2.5-point underdogs in Houston with Burrow's back still questionable. I said 52% for Rob looked stingy. I'm saying it louder.

I called the Lions the decoration at someone else's housewarming, and Josh Allen hung them on the wall himself. He scored five touchdowns in a 41-31 Bills win to open the new Highmark Stadium. Compton said beforehand that the Lions' defense was "in trouble", which turned out to be the politest available description. Scoring 31 and losing by ten is a defense that ends bets, Andy, and you hold it in all three of yours. Avonte Maddox left in the second quarter with a foot injury, so the secondary that gave up 41 is now thinner. The market pushed Detroit out from +1900 to +2000. I think that's generous. Andy came in as the underdog against everybody, and my hunch is those numbers are heading south today.

Now, Darren. Yesterday I gave you a rookie with four pressures as the entire Bengals case. Today Joe Burrow is questionable with back tightness, and Compton says that as a Bengals fan he "would be afraid." Cincinnati's next stop is a Texans defense that Will Anderson says just got its "wake-up call." Rob's 52% in that bet looks stingy to me.

Rob and Darren shouldn't get smug about Baltimore. I said the receivers looked like a problem. Ja'Kobi Lane is now on injured reserve and Zay Flowers is questionable with a hamstring. Stanley, Hendrickson and Madubuike are all questionable too. The Ravens drifted from +900 to +920, which is small, but a team with no real problems doesn't carry an injury list that long. Steve, your only worry is Chris Jones's calf, and you're sitting prettiest by doing nothing. That's very on brand.

Andy is the only man in this pool holding the Lions, which means Andy is the only man in this pool with no one to share the blame with. Stephen A. says the defense is a huge concern; I'd go further and say it's the kind of concern that ends bets in October. Pacheco is gone for twelve weeks after back surgery, which leaves Gibbs carrying what the coaches cheerfully call a "big workload" and what I call a countdown clock with hamstrings. And the reward for all this? A primetime trip to Buffalo's shiny new stadium, where the Lions get to be the decoration at someone else's housewarming. Andy, my condolences, respectfully.

Rob and Darren are both sitting on Baltimore against Andy and Steve, which is the smartest thing either of them has done all year, and I suspect entirely by accident. Emmitt Smith is out here admitting Derrick Henry might take his record, and the Ravens' biggest operational decision this week was releasing a kicker because the other kicker was too good. That is a team with no real problems, unless you count the receivers, and the receivers do look like a problem.

Steve's Chiefs beat everyone but Rob and Darren's Ravens on paper — Kenneth Walker looked genuinely good in his debut — though Greeny has already flip-flopped and Stephen A. won't crown them, which is about as close to a warning sign as September offers. Darren also holds the Bengals against Rob. A rookie got four pressures. That's the whole case. Good luck with it, Darren.

Steve is insufferable this week and he has earned it: Kansas City opened with a blowout of Denver, Mahomes back from the torn ACL and Kenneth Walker III looking the part on debut. That's the Chiefs card he holds over Rob, Andy and Darren all at once. Mild comfort for the rest: Stephen A. still won't call Kansas City the team to beat in the AFC, and Greeny has already changed his mind about the Broncos and Chiefs — whatever that's worth in September.

Rob and Darren split the Ravens between them, and Baltimore's news is fiddly rather than dire — Jake Moody cut loose after Tyler Loop's strong opener, and receiver worries with Zay Flowers day-to-day and Ja'Kobi Lane out longer with a wrist.

Andy has Detroit against everybody, so he owns all of it: Isiah Pacheco is out roughly twelve weeks after back surgery, Jahmyr Gibbs is being lined up for a heavy workload, Stephen A. has decided the defense is a concern, and the Lions walk into Buffalo's new stadium in prime time. Darren's Bengals beat, against Rob only, is rookie Howell's four pressures in a win. Quietly the best week of anyone's.
